doc.title: Ray Bauduc and Nappy Lamare Interview, 1959-09-09

title: Nappy on banjo influences: Stale Bread, a riverboat kid, Lou Black
summary: Nappy says he had no favorite banjo players. He recalls Stale Bread, a young Black banjoist on a boat, and Lou Black of the Rhythm Kings in Chicago as inspirations.

story.theme_name: Banjo, guitar and the rhythm section: instruments and players
story.community_name: Banjo, guitar and the rhythm section's changing role

blocks.x: Who were your favorite banjo players, Nappy? Well, really, I... There were none. Did you ever hear of Stale Bread? Yeah, yeah, yeah.
He was a guitar player, but they made homemade instruments, I think, too.

Do you remember him? I never got to know him. I imagine there was some kid on a boat, a colored kid, played a real fine banjo. I don't even remember his name. And he sort of inspired me a little. And also this banjo player with the Rhythm Kings. I don't remember his name. Louis Black. Louis Black. Oh, yeah. In Chicago. Yeah. He played wonderful. Yeah, well, that's...
